title: Two passes: story first, words second
summary: Read a passage twice with different goals so guessing and looking up do not fight each other.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: Guessing from context and checking in a dictionary are different jobs, and doing both in one pass slows each down. On the first read, go all the way to the end and allow yourself to guess; mark nothing. On the second read, stop only at words that block the meaning and look them up, ignoring the ones you could guess. This order teaches your brain to build a situation first, which is what a real reader does, and it stops a short text from becoming an hour of reference work.
